issues.note: The no-past-form/had to fact repeats across fields; the must/have to contrast is suitably hedged.
Obligation example sits under the almost-certainly-true sense.
Same misplaced obligation example, correctly filed under examples_fit.
Interrogative must is sense 1 in question form, not a missing use; wrong field too.
Adaptation note only restates the explanation, usage note and learner errors.
Shall is not an American English synonym of obligation must outside legal texts.
Must takes a bare infinitive; the to-infinitive pattern is wrong.
Inferential will (that'll be Sam) is a fair comparison for epistemic must.
The abbreviation e.g. is banned in prose.
Questions with must belong to sense 1 grammar; not a separate missing use.
The to-infinitive pattern contradicts the examples and the learner-error note.

findings.F1: senses[0].grammar gives the pattern 'verb + to-infinitive', but must takes a bare infinitive.
findings.F2: The obligation example 'You must hand in your homework by Friday.' is placed under the almost-certainly-true sense.
findings.F3: shall-modal is listed as a synonym of obligation must, which it is not in present-day American English.
findings.F4: The facts that must has no past form (use had to) and that must not differs from don't have to are repeated across the explanation, usage note, learner errors and grammar adaptation note.
findings.F5: The usage note uses the banned abbreviation 'e.g.'.
